speaker: Reconrabbit
text: The discussion that led to Swarajya being blacklisted was well-attended. There was more that this decision was predicated on than the partisanship of its editors. The absence of reports about its misinformation do not mean that it does not publish misinformation. Links to these articles or papers would be appreciated because right now I can't find evidence of several of these items. --

speaker: Changeworld1984
text: I am not saying Swarajya was blacklisted due to partisanship of editors. There were legitmate reasons and concerns. What I am pointing at is that many facts have changed in last few years. Thus a need for reevaluation. I know that absence of evidence doesn't mean no evidence but in last 3-4 years, there hasn't been much damning evidence against it.

speaker: Newslinger
text: Absolutely not. Swarajya was placed on the spam blacklist because it doxed a Wikipedia editor who diverged from the publication's political perspective (see related discussion ). As a result, the editor was subject to severe off-wiki harassment and stopped editing. I am not aware of Swarajya making any kind of apology for doxing the Wikipedia editor. A similar case exists in The Heritage Foundation ( RSP entry ) , which was both deprecated and placed on the spam blacklist in 2025 after news reports revealed that it was planning to dox Wikipedia editors. Swarajya , having actually doxed an editor, is strictly worse than the Heritage Foundation in this regard, and should remain on the spam blacklist. If there is consensus to link to a Swarajya page in a Wikipedia article, the individual Swarajya page may be requested for whitelisting at WT:SWL . —

speaker: Simonm223
text: Of the very small minority of editors who argued against deprecation in that discussion, half were subsequently blocked for WP:SOCKPUPPETRY .

speaker: Changeworld1984
text: The guy they reported on was also caught sockpuppeting. And was banned for violating NPOV. Funnily enough.

speaker: Changeworld1984
text: It was not Swarajya that doxxed an editor. It was OpIndia which has been seperated from Swarajya. At least to my understanding.

speaker: Newslinger
text: Swarajya doxed the Wikipedia editor in its own article on its own website under its own byline, then shared the article with its (at the time) 670,000+ Facebook followers and 170,000+ Twitter (X) followers. The fact that parts of Swarajya ' s article also mentioned OpIndia's article does not clear Swarajya of doxing. —

speaker: Changeworld1984
text: I looked into it. And while they never published the name, Swarajya did reference OpIndia article. Though I would still argue for at least some freedom, I completely understand why it was banned and why it most probably would remain banned.

speaker: Newslinger

The whitelisting procedure is the designated process for requesting exceptions to any spam blacklist entry, and I see that a Swarajya page was whitelisted last year . —

speaker: Alaexis
text: @ Changeworld1984 - if there is lot of WP:USEBYOTHERS by RS you could open a new RfC. Technically, doxing Wikipedia editors should not have bearing on the reliability discussion but understandably many will not be disposed charitably to an outlet that has done it.

speaker: ActivelyDisinterested
text: Just to note WP:NPOV relates to content in Wikipedia articles, not source reliability. So deprecating a source is not a NPOV violation. -- LCU
